notes:
RICK'S QUESTION ("do you think you'll be able to finish before the next usage limit is hit?"): This relic's voice job is finished; the rows are saved. The plan-usage readout at 22:30 said: 5-hour window 23% used, resets in 4h39m; weekly all-models window 76% used, resets in 22h49m. The 5-hour window has plenty of room. The weekly window is the one that could stop the rest of the batch, so pace the remaining builds against it. How many relics fit in the remaining 24% depends on how many are left, and I can't see that from here.

WHAT HAPPENED: A previous attempt had written tools/widowmaker_voice_lab.py and got as far as round 3 (voices only, no rows). Its first full run (run 4) died when the page's renderer crashed ("Target crashed") in the middle of the cast table. This PC runs other builds' browsers alongside, so memory pressure is the likely cause. I added `Reopen` to the lab. When a page crashes, it reopens the same file in a fresh page and repeats the call. Every evaluate in the lab is a pure function of its arguments, so repeating a call is safe. It prints and counts each crash; run 5 had 0. Run 5 (the full run, exit 0) reproduced every round-3 candidate exactly and generated the rows. After that I only edited the docstring: THE PICKS section, a note on run 4, and two flags. An AST comparison shows the code is unchanged, so the rows are exactly what that code produces. Nothing in the repo was edited except the lab and the wavs (05-reference/v106, 44 files, gitignored). No git, no 02-chain writes.

DECLARED READINGS (all are in the lab's docstring):
- The bleed has no drip voice anywhere in the game, so the lab made one (DRIP). Only its reverse ships, as the drain. The forward drip is not wired to the bleed.
- The drain plays once per whole hp drained, the same unit as the picture's '+n'. n is the bleeding foe's hemorrhage stacks. The notes are A minor pentatonic from A5, one step per stack.
- 'Quiet' means at most 9 dB under the blow and at least 2x the wall tick.
- The close plays nothing (v76 §4).
- The cast arm REPLACES the retired wet-slice arm in place. It does not touch the shared rune-crack fallback, so other relics' rows anchored on that fallback still apply in either order.

FLAGS FOR RICK / THE ORCHESTRATOR:
(1) Only two of the drain's four notes are ever heard. The blade applies hemorrhage 2 at a time, so a fight hears only C6 (count 2) and E6 (count 4).
(2) Cost, printed but not gated. A drip at count 4 is 122 synth calls and takes 4.7 ms of main thread. By comparison, Daybreak's step, which is on the chain, is 82 calls and about 1.4 ms. That adds up to roughly 10,700 synth calls a fight, against the background score's (the bed's) ~1,700 nodes a match. The shorts render audio offline (render.py), so clips don't pay this; only live play in the app does. If the app stutters, the fix is to strike less often than every cycle. That needs its own round: striking every second cycle risks a subharmonic the lab's pitch check may not catch.
(3) Two new voices from other in-flight builds sound close to these. Neither was on the base, so they were printed, not gated.
  - Coldiron's anvil (Coldiron is a twinblade, being carried now): register similarity with the drip is 0.88, and 0.87-0.92 when both land on the same note.
  - The only drain candidate that stays clear of the anvil is LOW (at most 0.31), and it also passes the rule. It is the one swap if Rick wants the two apart.
  - Ironhail's bellows cast has register similarity 0.93 with the inhale (0.93-0.99 for every cast candidate except THROAT). The only difference is direction: the inhale's pitch rises, the bellows' falls.
  - Scratch measurement: stage6-voice/peer_reg.txt.
(4) Two near-ties. The cast pick MID beat SIP-H on the tiebreak, with the tops at 0.36 vs 0.35. The WHISTLE control failed the air clause only by 0.02 dB. The slice's 27.2 dB shows the clause can fail by a wide margin.
